info.description: Reusable authentication service. Cookie sessions require HTTPS. All auth mutations require an exact allowed Origin. CORS is opt-in; cookie profile is same-site.
info.title: Auth API

get.description: Public-only deployment key set. Contains no private signing material. Not an authorization decision. Keys are operator-controlled and loaded on startup.

head.description: Public-only deployment key set. Contains no private signing material. Not an authorization decision. Keys are operator-controlled and loaded on startup.

post.description: Requires a permanent password, verified email, enrolled MFA and current administrative authority. Always returns an MFA challenge, never a session. Complete with /api/v1/auth/mfa/login/complete. Independent of public login method settings; does not create an account or assign roles. Uses the public password login rate budget.
post.summary: Start administrative password and MFA login

400.description: codes: invalid_json, email_required, password_required, invalid_email, invalid_credentials

get.description: Requires a live session and auth.settings.manage. availableMethods describes adapters on this instance only. No secrets are returned; does not refresh the session.

post.description: Full non-secret policy replacement. Every boolean is required, including false. Requires auth.settings.manage, fresh password and MFA. expectedVersion prevents lost updates; adapters must be ready locally and identically configured on every instance. Existing sessions are not revoked.

get.description: Live session, HTTPS Origin and auth.settings.manage; no fresh proof for reading. Presence is not a live provider test. Redirect URI and fixed issuer/endpoints remain deployment configuration.
get.summary: Read Google or Telegram client settings without the secret

post.description: Requires auth.settings.manage, fresh password+MFA and expectedVersion. Omitted/null secret preserves it; explicit empty clears only while the method is disabled. Client ID change requires explicit secret, disabled method and no linked identities. Rotation invalidates pending OIDC/MFA/enrollment/recovery proofs, not existing sessions. No external connection under SQL locks.
post.summary: Configure or rotate Google/Telegram client credentials

parameters.description: client ID, expectedVersion and optional new secret
parameters.name: body

get.description: Requires a live session, allowed HTTPS Origin and auth.settings.manage. No fresh proof is required for reading. Durations are in days; worker batch and interval remain deployment configuration.

post.description: Requires auth.settings.manage, fresh password+MFA and expectedVersion. All periods must be 1..106751 days. Shortening any period requires confirmShortening=true and can cause irreversible deletion. Each subsequent worker batch reads current SQL settings; an already started batch can use the old snapshot within its five-second deadline. Existing session deadlines and transient challenge expiry do not change.

parameters.description: Complete retention policy and current version
parameters.name: body

get.description: Requires a live session, HTTPS Origin and auth.settings.manage. passwordSet is presence only. No secrets, session refresh or network tests.
get.summary: Read SMTP settings without the password

post.description: Requires auth.settings.manage and fresh password+MFA. Full config replacement, explicit requireTls. Omitted/null password preserves it; empty clears it only without username. Changed destination/username requires explicit password. SMTP_ALLOWED_TARGETS is deployment-only; production cannot disable TLS. No network request in this transaction.
post.summary: Replace SMTP settings and optionally rotate the password

post.description: Requires auth.settings.manage and fresh password+MFA. Tests the authorized saved version only, after releasing SQL locks; greeting/STARTTLS/AUTH/NOOP, not actual delivery. Max 10 seconds, 3/user/minute and 10/project/minute, 2 concurrent tests/instance. Does not store a readiness claim or refresh the session.
post.summary: Test the saved SMTP connection without sending email

get.description: Requires current access.roles.manage or access.assignments.manage. Returns declared keys, not an ability to create arbitrary permissions through HTTP.

Requires current roles.manage or assignments.manage. Keyset pagination, no count or per-role permission queries. A full page returns its last key as nextAfter; a final empty page may be necessary. Use role detail for permissions.

post.description: Requires access.roles.manage, all delegated permissions and fresh password plus MFA in the mutation transaction. No system role or wildcard bypass. Duplicate key returns conflict; no automatic assignments.

get.description: Requires current access.roles.manage or access.assignments.manage. Includes version for a subsequent explicit edit or assignment. Reads do not renew session or authentication freshness.
get.summary: Read a role and its permissions

post.description: Replaces the definition; omitted/null mfaRequired preserves its previous value for older clients. Requires access.roles.manage, old and new delegated permissions, fresh password plus MFA and current role version in one transaction. Enabling required MFA invalidates old role-bound sessions. A no-op preserves the version; system roles cannot be changed.

get.description: Requires current accounts.users.read and SQL session; no fresh password/MFA or session renewal for this read. Newest createdAt/UUID first, exclusive cursor, nondeleted users only. Exact normalized email and optional status filters, no substring search, offset or total count. Selected display email prefers password contact, otherwise first retained contact by UUID. One bounded SQL statement checks permission and reads a page.

parameters.description: Opaque exclusive nextCursor from the previous page
parameters.name: before

post.description: Requires INVITATIONS_ENABLED, MFA_ENABLED, accounts.users.manage and fresh password plus MFA checked in the write transaction, including replay. Actor comes only from the current session. UUID idempotency key is scoped by actor; mismatched parameters or occupied email conflict. No roles, verified email, password or session are granted. Replay does not resend mail or reactivate the account.
post.summary: Create a pending user, optionally with an email invitation

parameters.description: UUID command key; email required when invite=true
parameters.name: body

post.description: Requires TEMPORARY_PASSWORD_ENABLED, MFA_ENABLED, accounts.users.manage and current fresh password plus MFA. Independent of invitations. Server generates the secret; response contains password only on first commit. Replay never returns it or extends TTL. No email verification, roles or session. Protect the response, do not log or cache it. Lost response requires a new reissue command after cooldown.
post.summary: Create a pending user with a one-time temporary password

parameters.description: UUID command key and unoccupied email
parameters.name: body

200.description: Replay without password or original expiresAt

get.description: Requires current accounts.users.read, not a user UUID claim or management permission alone. Includes stored status/versions, contact verification, configured password/MFA, external issuers and role metadata. Configuration is not a guarantee of usable login or effective access. No password hash, subject, token, MFA secret or recovery codes. UUID lookup also supports retained soft-deleted users without restoring them. Contacts/providers/roles bounded to 32; overflow is an explicit conflict, not silent truncation.

delete.description: Requires MFA_ENABLED, accounts.users.delete and fresh password plus MFA in the deletion transaction. Actor comes only from the session. Current authVersion is mandatory; stale retries conflict, a retry with the current tombstone version is a no-op but still requires authorization. Uses existing atomic credential cleanup, session revocation, audit and email reservation policy. This is a retained tombstone, not complete PII erasure. No account restoration. Last system administrator is protected.

get.description: Requires current access.assignments.manage. UUID lookup only, no user enumeration. One SQL statement checks actor session/permission and reads the target. Unknown/deleted target and unauthorized actor share forbidden. Pending/blocked targets may have assignments but cannot exercise permissions. accessVersion is for assignment concurrency, not permission caching.
get.summary: Read a user's role assignments and permission union

post.description: Requires current super_admin membership, access.assignments.manage, all delegated system-role permissions and fresh password plus MFA in one transaction. No self-grant or arbitrary system role. Target must be active, have a permanent password, verified login email and enrolled TOTP, with no pending activation/temporary credentials. Requires current target auth/access and system role versions. Does not create credentials, a session, a new role or a bootstrap bypass. Authorized current-version replay is a no-op.

parameters.description: Current target auth/access and super_admin role versions
parameters.name: body

delete.description: Requires current super_admin membership, access.assignments.manage, delegated system-role permissions and fresh password plus MFA. Current target auth/access and role versions are checked in the same transaction. Preserves another active administrator with permanent password, verified login email, enrolled TOTP and no pending/temporary activation. Self-revoke is allowed only with such a backup. Access changes immediately; no-op replay still requires current authority. Does not delete the account, disable MFA or change the system role itself.

parameters.description: Current target auth/access and super_admin role versions
parameters.name: body

post.description: Requires accounts.email.bind and fresh password plus MFA in SQL. Explicit target UUID, active external-only account without contacts. Sends a code but does not reserve/attach the address, create an account or bypass the owner's MFA. Approval expires no later than the administrator's current authentication proof.
post.summary: Approve a user's initial email binding

post.description: Requires accounts.users.manage and fresh password plus MFA; current SQL authority is checked on reads, writes and replay. UUID command key, original unverified contact, pending provisioned user only. No email changes, new user, roles, session or bypass of temporary-password activation. Cooldown and Redis budgets apply. Replay does not send another message.
post.summary: Reissue a pending user's email invitation

parameters.description: New command key, or the same key for a retry
parameters.name: body

post.description: Requires access.assignments.manage, all delegated role permissions, current role/access versions and fresh password plus MFA in one transaction. No self-grant or system-role assignment. Pending users receive access only after activation. Retry with stale versions returns conflict; a current no-op preserves the version.
post.summary: Assign a custom role to a user

parameters.description: Expected role and user assignment versions
parameters.name: body

delete.description: JSON body is required also for DELETE. Same permission/delegation/version/password/MFA transaction guard as grant. Self-revoke of a custom role is allowed; system role cannot be revoked. Subsequent authorization uses current SQL assignments.
delete.summary: Revoke a custom role from a user

parameters.description: Expected role and user assignment versions
parameters.name: body

post.description: Requires MFA_ENABLED, accounts.users.status.manage and fresh password plus MFA checked in the mutation transaction. Actor is derived from the current session. Requires current authVersion; changes revoke sessions and outstanding activation/recovery proofs. Unblocking does not activate pending users, restore deleted accounts or revive old sessions. Last system administrator is protected. Read/create permissions do not authorize this operation.

Requires accounts.users.manage and current fresh password plus MFA on both preflight/replay and mutation. Only an existing pending temporary-password account, original unverified contact and cooldown; does not reset an active user's password. First commit returns a new secret once and invalidates old temporary/setup authority. Replay preserves stored expiry and never returns password. No email, roles or session are granted.
post.summary: Reissue a pending user's temporary password

get.description: Current SQL role IDs, known permissions and assignment version, for this authenticated user only. The version is not a cache key for role contents. This response helps UI presentation; the backend must authorize every protected operation itself.

post.description: Requires a valid SQL-backed __Host-session, verified login email, allowed Origin and current password. Atomically updates password, revokes all sessions and records audit; sign in again. Response retains legacy uppercase Status. MFA is not implemented.

400.description: codes: password_policy, invalid_json, password_mismatch, invalid_email_or_password, same_password, empty_new_password, empty_old_password, empty_confirm_password

post.description: Requires the requesting browser flow cookie, eight decimal digits, allowed Origin, current status/version/email and at most five failed guesses per challenge. One-time consumption then ordinary SQL session issuance; not MFA or password reauthentication.
post.summary: Sign in with a one-time email code

202.description: MFA required; browser binding cookie, no session issued

post.description: Optional profile, existing active account with verified current password email only. Generic accepted response; sets a browser-bound HttpOnly flow cookie. Does not register, verify email or create a session.
post.summary: Request a passwordless email login code

post.description: Requires the target's live session, mailed eight-digit code and fresh MFA if a factor is enrolled. Rechecks the approving administrator's current password/MFA/session/permission in SQL. Atomically creates a verified contact, raises auth_version, revokes all target sessions and records audit. Does not create login authority or merge accounts.
post.summary: Confirm the owner's initial email binding

post.description: Optional EMAIL_CHANGE_ENABLED profile. Requires a valid session, allowed Origin, verified current login email and either current password or recent session-bound password reauthentication. Omit password after successful reauthentication; a supplied wrong password is always rejected. Old email remains active until confirmation. Sends separate confirmation and security links; no tokens returned.

parameters.description: new email, optional current password when already reauthenticated
parameters.name: body

post.description: Optional profile. Explicit POST with a purpose-bound one-time token. Original session must still be valid. Claims new email, revokes all sessions and sends old-address notice atomically. No session created; GET links never mutate state.

Optional password-only profile. Distinct single-use token delivered to the old verified address after protective blocking. Atomically replaces the compromised password, restores that address, revokes access and invalidates previous protection links before activating the account. Does not bypass administrative blocking, create a session or run on GET.
post.summary: Recover an account after an unauthorized email change

400.description: codes: invalid_json, invalid_account_recovery, password_mismatch, password_policy, same_password

post.description: Optional profile. Explicit POST with a distinct old-verified-address one-time token; does not require the compromised session. Cancels pending change and revokes sessions, or blocks the account after completion. Never rolls back email, unblocks or signs in automatically. Protected recovery remains a separate release gate.
Always returns accepted for unknown, verified, blocked and cooldown addresses. Enqueues encrypted delivery for eligible addresses. Limits use socket peer IP; forwarded headers are not trusted.
Consumes a 256-bit token once. Expired, replaced, replayed, blocked or unknown tokens share one error. Does not create a session. POST only; opening an email link must not confirm automatically.
Generic accepted response for unknown, blocked and cooldown addresses. Enqueues an encrypted email after SQL commit; does not guarantee delivery. Socket IP limits; forwarded headers are not trusted.

get.description: Provider redirect bound to single-use state, PKCE, nonce and flow cookie. Login sets __Host-session; linking requires the unchanged fresh session and never creates or replaces it. No email auto-merge. Restart after a failed or lost callback.

202.description: MFA required; browser binding cookie, no session issued

post.description: Requires current session, exact Origin, verified email with permanent password and recent password reauthentication. Flow binds UUID and session hash; callback does not create a session or user. One identity per provider per account.
post.summary: Start linking Google to the current account

delete.description: Requires Origin and fresh password proof. A verified permanent password login must remain. Successful unlink increments auth_version and revokes all sessions, including the caller. Unknown ownership is not revealed.
delete.summary: Unlink Google from the current account

post.description: Requires allowed Origin. Sets a browser-bound HttpOnly flow cookie; navigate to authorizationUrl. Disabled by default.

Optional invitation profile. Consumes a distinct one-time token, sets a password and verifies the invited contact atomically. Expired, replayed, blocked and unknown tokens have one error. Does not create a session or assign roles. GET never activates an account.

Sets the Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax __Host-session cookie on success, or returns an MFA challenge. Current saved password policy is rechecked in the final SQL commit; required email verification refuses unverified credentials without a session. HTTPS and allowed Origin are required. Invalid credentials return 400, not 401. Disabling a method does not revoke already issued sessions.

202.description: MFA required; browser binding cookie, no session issued

400.description: codes: invalid_json, email_required, password_required, invalid_email, invalid_credentials

post.description: Missing or invalid sessions return 401 and clear the stale cookie. Dependency failures do not clear it. Requires an allowed Origin.
post.summary: Revoke current session and clear browser cookie

post.description: Requires an allowed Origin. Auth version increment prevents stale in-flight issuance.
post.summary: Revoke all own sessions including current and clear browser cookie

get.description: Requires __Host-session cookie. Returns IDs only; profile and contact management are separate features.
get.summary: Get authenticated user and current session IDs

post.description: Requires the same browser binding cookie and allowed Origin. Consumes TOTP/recovery and challenge atomically with SQL session issuance. No client UUID, auth version or MFA timestamp is accepted.
post.summary: Complete login with a second factor

post.description: Accepts only an enrollment-required primary challenge with the same browser binding. No full session, account UUID or password is accepted. Secret expires with the existing login challenge; restarting does not extend its deadline.
post.summary: Start mandatory TOTP enrollment during login

post.description: Requires the primary challenge, browser binding, enrollment token and first TOTP. Commits the factor, recovery codes, auth_version and revocation atomically; returns codes once. Creates no session: sign in again with primary plus MFA.
post.summary: Confirm mandatory TOTP enrollment during login

parameters.description: Challenge, enrollment token and first code
parameters.name: body

post.description: Requires fresh primary and MFA proofs. Primary is password, or opt-in verified-email proof for an external-only account. Replaces all recovery codes, returns ten new codes once and revokes sessions/pending challenges atomically. TOTP remains enabled.

Requires the same primary challenge/browser, exact current operator-approved request and new TOTP. Rechecks method/status/version/operator identity and membership. Atomically replaces factor/recovery codes, revokes sessions and records audit/durable verified-contact notification. Returns codes once, clears old cookies, never issues a session or disables MFA. Expired, unapproved, cancelled, foreign and replayed requests share invalid_mfa. Five wrong codes exhaust the request and account guessing budget is shared with normal MFA login. Missing verified contact requires independent operator notification.

parameters.description: request, primary challenge and new TOTP
parameters.name: body

404.description: method_disabled for public primary; route absent when recovery disabled

post.description: Opt-in MFA_RECOVERY_ENABLED. Requires a live primary login challenge, its single browser cookie and allowed Origin, not a session. Returns a new candidate once; old MFA stays active. Reissue discards old approval without extending the primary TTL. Independent owner verification and CLI approval are required before completion. No user UUID, actor, version or approved flag accepted.

404.description: method_disabled for public primary; route absent when recovery disabled

get.description: Live owner-only snapshot, no fresh proof required. No secrets, recovery code values, session refresh or audit. Availability is local, not SMTP/fleet health. Policy flags are informational; mutations independently recheck current state and proof.
get.summary: Read own MFA status and policy

post.description: Requires fresh password proof, or opt-in verified-email proof for an external-only account, within five minutes. Consumes TOTP/recovery, rotates the current session verifier and records fresh MFA context atomically. Does not extend session lifetime.

delete.description: Requires fresh primary and MFA proofs. Primary is password, or opt-in verified-email proof for an external-only account. Administrative-role policy cannot be bypassed. Removes recovery codes, raises auth_version and revokes all sessions atomically.
delete.summary: Disable TOTP for the current account

post.description: Requires an active session and fresh password proof, or opt-in verified-email proof for an external-only account, within five minutes. Returns the secret once in a no-store owner response. Does not enable MFA before confirmation.
Consumes the first code, returns ten recovery codes once, raises auth_version and revokes all sessions atomically. Sign in again with MFA; no session is created here.

Requires fresh primary and MFA proofs. Primary is password, or opt-in verified-email proof for an external-only account. The current factor remains usable until confirmation. Replacement cannot use an ordinary enrollment token.

Requires the unchanged fresh primary/MFA session, replacement token and a code from the new factor. Primary is password, or opt-in verified-email proof for an external-only account. Replaces secret/recovery codes, raises auth_version and revokes all sessions atomically.

Native client only. One-use binding/code, not a browser challenge. Audience/scope come only from stored request. Email code is the primary method, not MFA. If issuance fails after code consumption, request a new code; no retry/grace or intermediate cookie session.
post.summary: Sign in with a native email code

post.description: Native client only, no Origin/Cookie/Authorization/query. Neutral accepted response for unknown or ineligible accounts; code only for eligible existing accounts. Store the returned binding in protected client memory. Audience/scope are bound server-side. No browser flow cookie.
post.summary: Request a native email login code

post.description: Cookie-free native challenge only, never browser/private-admin proof. Recovery defaults to false (TOTP); true selects one recovery code. Factor consumption, session/family issuance and audit commit atomically. Parallel/replayed attempts cannot create independent successors. No Origin/Cookie/Authorization/query.

Only a native enrollment-required primary challenge and its binding. No Origin/Cookie/Authorization/query. Returns the enrollment secret once for setup, no access or refresh credentials. Repeating start does not extend the primary challenge deadline.

Commits TOTP, recovery codes, version bump and revocation together. Codes returned once. Does not issue tokens: perform a fresh primary login then MFA. Native challenge/binding only; no Origin/Cookie/Authorization/query or cookie mutations.

parameters.description: Primary challenge, native binding, enrollment token and first TOTP
parameters.name: body

post.description: Cookie-free native client only: Origin, Cookie, Authorization and query parameters are rejected. JSON <=8 KiB. Uses current password policy and primary checks. Required MFA/enrollment returns only a bound restricted challenge. No browser session is created. Strict JWT use requires an online authority check at the consumer.
post.summary: Sign in to the native API with a password

post.description: Same owner/session/version and one-time flow cookie; rotates the existing session token atomically without extending lifetime. Grants a five-minute email proof, not password proof, MFA proof or administrative permissions. Existing MFA is still required to replace or disable a factor.
post.summary: Confirm an email proof for MFA management

post.description: Optional, existing external-only account with an active session and an already verified owned email. Does not attach or verify a new address, authenticate by password or issue a new session.
post.summary: Request an email proof for MFA management

post.description: Requires current session cookie and allowed Origin. Atomically rotates the token and records password proof for this session only. Does not extend session deadlines, prove MFA or grant permissions. No old-token grace period; serialize requests around reauthentication. Lost successful response requires login. Password and token never returned in JSON.
post.summary: Confirm current password for sensitive actions

post.description: Enforces current public method/registration policy. Required email verification returns 201 with verificationRequired=true and no session cookie. Optional queues verification and issues a session; disabled does not queue automatic verification or mark the address verified. Account and queued mail commit atomically; session issuance is separate, so an error does not prove account rollback. A committed retry returns 409, never automatic login. HTTPS and allowed Origin are required.

400.description: codes: invalid_json, email_required, password_required, invalid_email, password_too_short, password_too_long, password_no_letter, password_no_digit, password_no_upper_letter

post.description: Single-use 256-bit token. SQL commit atomically updates the password, consumes the token, revokes all sessions and records audit. Does not verify email or create a session; sign in again. New password: 8-128 bytes, letter, digit and uppercase. POST only, never automatic GET confirmation.

Call only after user interaction, never from polling or timers alone. Administrative sessions use a stored bounded idle window; ordinary sessions are unchanged. Does not renew primary, password or MFA proof or the absolute deadline. No body or client timestamps.

Requires an allowed Origin and the current session cookie. Replaces the token once without extending deadlines or refreshing authentication. Concurrent rotations have one winner; serialize browser requests around rotation. A lost successful response requires a new login. No old-token grace period.

get.description: Up to 50 items ordered by creation time and public UUID descending; pass nextCursor as before. No session secrets are returned.

delete.description: Foreign, unknown and inactive sessions share 404. Revoking current session also clears the cookie. Requires an allowed Origin.

get.description: Provider redirect bound to single-use state, PKCE, nonce and flow cookie. Login sets __Host-session; linking requires the unchanged fresh session and never creates or replaces it. No email auto-merge. Restart after a failed or lost callback.

202.description: MFA required; browser binding cookie, no session issued

post.description: Requires current session, exact Origin, verified email with permanent password and recent password reauthentication. Flow binds UUID and session hash; callback does not create a session or user. One identity per provider per account.
post.summary: Start linking Telegram to the current account

delete.description: Requires Origin and fresh password proof. A verified permanent password login must remain. Successful unlink increments auth_version and revokes all sessions, including the caller. Unknown ownership is not revealed.
delete.summary: Unlink Telegram from the current account

post.description: Requires allowed Origin. Sets a browser-bound HttpOnly flow cookie; navigate to authorizationUrl. Disabled by default.

Optional temporary password profile. Consumes a one-time setup token and revokes temporary credentials atomically. Does not create a session, verify email, bypass MFA or grant roles. Use ordinary login afterwards. GET never changes credentials.
post.summary: Set a permanent password after temporary login

400.description: codes: invalid_json, invalid_temporary_password, password_mismatch, password_policy, same_password

post.description: Optional temporary password profile. Returns only a short-lived password-setup token, never a session cookie. Repeated successful login replaces the previous setup token. Does not verify email or grant product access. Shares ordinary login rate limits.

400.description: codes: invalid_json, email_required, password_required, invalid_email, invalid_temporary_password

post.description: Requires exact allowed Origin and a live completed cookie session. Does not refresh the session or MFA. Scope is restricted by the configured audience and current SQL grants. Strict tokens still require an online authority decision at the consumer.
post.summary: Issue an access JWT from the current cookie session

post.description: Native JSON credential only; no Origin/Cookie/Authorization/query. Repeated or unknown well-formed refresh returns 204. A known current or spent credential revokes only its own family; never logout-all. Does not remove reuse history. Local JWTs remain valid until their published expiry window; strict consumers require online authority.
post.summary: Revoke the native refresh family and its API session

post.description: Native JSON credential only; no Origin/Cookie/Authorization/query. Single-flight required. Replay of a known spent credential commits family/session revocation before 401. No retry/grace on lost responses. First rotation can be immediate, later >=30s; 4096 credentials/family, then sign in again. Does not extend absolute lifetime, scope or assurance.
post.summary: Rotate native refresh and issue an access token

post.description: Dev-only endpoint for manual SMTP testing. Available only when APP_ENV=dev.

Service-to-service HTTPS only. Dedicated per-consumer HTTP Basic credentials, not user Bearer/cookies. Invalid/inactive tokens return only active:false. Does not renew sessions. Custom protocol, not RFC 7662.
post.summary: Check an access JWT against current session authority

parameters.description: Basic service client ID and secret
parameters.name: Authorization

post.description: Consumes installation proof and pending intent with email and TOTP codes. Atomically creates account, verified contact, factor, recovery codes, system grant and durable initialized marker. Returns recovery codes once; does not issue a session. Setup stays closed after restart or loss of administrator.
post.summary: Complete first administrator setup exactly once

post.description: Requires installation operator secret and allowed HTTPS Origin. Sends email code. Returns bounded setup token and TOTP enrollment data, not a login session. No user exists yet. A retry after one minute replaces previous intent.
